_comment: CliniX media registry AND licence gate. Nothing renders unless cleared === true with a real licence and attribution. This mirrors atlas-pipeline/sources.json require_clear(): the registry REFUSES uncleared media rather than documenting the problem in a comment. Contrast assets/kardiox-learn/, which holds 872 images with no manifest and no licence record at all.
_howToClear: 1. Confirm the licence permits use in a commercial mobile app (CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA, public domain, or explicit permission).
2. For an embed, confirm the rights holder has left embedding enabled and that we link/iframe rather than re-host.
3. Fill licence, attribution, sourceUrl (and src for a hosted asset).
4. Set cleared: true. Only then does it render.
NEVER set cleared: true to make a screen look finished. An uncleared entry degrades to caption plus 'source pending', which is honest; a wrongly cleared one is a licence breach.
_status: Phase 1 ships the registry and the gate with the COPD work order below. No entry is cleared yet, so every lesson currently renders its caption and a 'visual pending' note rather than an asset. That is the gate working, not a bug.

media.resp.inspection.barrel.caption: Barrel-shaped chest: increased anteroposterior diameter seen from the side
media.resp.inspection.barrel.note: Needs an openly-licensed lateral photograph of a hyperinflated chest, or an owner-produced one with patient consent. Wikimedia Commons and Radiopaedia (CC BY-NC-SA, check commercial terms) are the first places to look.

media.resp.inspection.pursedlip.caption: Pursed-lip breathing and accessory muscle use
media.resp.inspection.pursedlip.note: Short clip. Owner-produced is the cleanest route: it is easy to demonstrate and needs no patient.

media.resp.inspection.hoover.caption: Hoover sign: inward movement of the lower costal margin on inspiration
media.resp.inspection.hoover.note: A short loop is far better than prose here. Consider an owner-produced animation rather than patient footage.

media.resp.expansion.technique.caption: Chest expansion: thumbs lifted clear of the chest wall
media.resp.expansion.technique.note: The single highest-value clip in the respiratory set, because the floating-thumb detail is what students get wrong and is almost impossible to convey in text.

media.resp.percussion.technique.caption: Percussion technique: pleximeter placement and a loose wrist
media.resp.percussion.technique.note: Owner-produced or a permitted embed. Must show the side-to-side comparison order, not just the striking action.

media.resp.auscultation.wheeze.caption: Polyphonic expiratory wheeze
media.resp.auscultation.wheeze.note: Audio is essential rather than decorative for added sounds. Look for openly-licensed teaching libraries; several university collections publish under CC. Verify commercial terms.

media.resp.auscultation.crackles_coarse.caption: Early coarse crackles that change with coughing
media.resp.auscultation.crackles_coarse.note: Pair with the fine late inspiratory crackle below, so the contrast can be heard back to back. The contrast is the lesson.

media.resp.auscultation.crackles_fine.caption: Fine late inspiratory crackles that do not clear with coughing
media.resp.auscultation.crackles_fine.note: Contrast pair for the coarse crackle above.

media.gen.clubbing.schamroth.caption: Schamroth window: normal diamond, and its loss in clubbing
media.gen.clubbing.schamroth.note: A side-by-side normal and abnormal is worth more than either alone. Wikimedia Commons has candidate images; confirm the specific file's licence, not the category's.

media.gen.cyanosis.central.caption: Central cyanosis of the tongue
media.gen.cyanosis.central.note: Needs a genuinely representative image; poor colour reproduction makes this actively misleading, so reject a marginal one.

media.copd.spirometry.curve.caption: Flow-volume loop in obstruction compared with normal
media.copd.spirometry.curve.note: Best drawn in-house as an SVG. A self-authored diagram sidesteps the licence question entirely and can be made theme-aware and interactive.

media.copd.pathophys.airtrapping.caption: Small airway collapse on expiration and gas trapping
media.copd.pathophys.airtrapping.note: Self-authored SVG animation. This is the mechanism most of the COPD signs derive from, so it earns a real animation.
